extracted_claims.text: Under the original text of the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were set to apply from 2 August 2026, with transitional provisions in Article 111 referencing operators of high-risk systems placed on the market before that date.

A legislative package known as the 'Digital Omnibus on AI' (also called the 'AI Omnibus') amended Article 113 of the AI Act to extend the application date for Annex III high-risk AI obligations to 2 December 2027.
The same Omnibus amendment extended the application date for high-risk AI systems that are products or safety components regulated under Annex I (Union harmonisation legislation) to 2 August 2028.

The AI Omnibus proposal was adopted by the Commission on 19 November 2025, a political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026, and the amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026.

The amended, consolidated text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (version dated 27 July 2026) no longer hardcodes 2 August 2026 for operators of pre-existing high-risk systems, instead referring generically to 'the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113', reflecting the Omnibus-extended timeline.

The amended Article 113 text shows that Chapters I and II apply from 2 February 2025; Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII, Chapter XII and Article 78 apply from 2 August 2025 (except Article 101); and Chapter III Sections 1, 2 and 3 (except Article 6(5)), which contain the Annex III high-risk obligations, apply from 2 December 2027, while the Regulation as a whole (the general catch-all provision) applies from 2 August 2026.

Separately from the Annex III timeline, prohibitions on unacceptable-risk AI practices and transparency obligations under Article 50 generally apply from 2 August 2026, with a transition until 2 December 2026 for certain legacy synthetic-content systems to comply with Article 50(2), and new prohibitions on non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM apply from 2 December 2026.

12 identical legal-analysis/news articles describe the 2 December 2027 Annex III date as 'confirmed' and 'binding' under a regulation referred to as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, part of the Digital Omnibus on AI.

A 2024-published European Parliament overview states that high-risk system obligations become applicable 36 months after entry into force of the AI Act (which entered into force 1 August 2024), rather than 24 months (i.e., around August 2027 rather than August 2026).

Some commentary (not law) characterizes 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 as 'backstop dates' that would apply by default if further amendments are not enacted, while cautioning that the applicable date 'in law today' before the Omnibus's entry into force was 2 August 2026.
A news/blog source dated April 2026 (before the Omnibus entered into force) still describes 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline for Annex III obligations.
Enforcement for non-compliance with high-risk obligations can carry penalties of up to €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover (or, per an older source, up to €35 million), whichever is higher.

# When Do Obligations for High-Risk AI Systems Under Annex III of the EU AI Act Start to Apply?

## Executive Summary
The application date for Annex III high-risk AI obligations has changed. Originally set at 2 August 2026, this deadline was extended to 2 December 2027 through a "Digital Omnibus on AI" amendment to Article 113, which entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence). A related, separate extension pushes the deadline for high-risk AI systems embedded as products/safety components under Annex I to 2 August 2028 (high confidence). Significant inconsistency remains across secondary sources, many of which still cite the superseded 2026 date.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
Under the original text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems were set to apply from 2 August 2026, with Article 111 governing transitional treatment of systems already placed on the market before that date ([AI Act Service Desk – Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)) (high confidence).

### The Omnibus Extension
A legislative package known as the "Digital Omnibus on AI" amended Article 113 to extend the Annex III application date to 2 December 2027 ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)) (high confidence). The same amendment extended the deadline for high-risk AI systems regulated as products/safety components under Annex I (Union harmonisation legislation) to 2 August 2028 ([Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)) (high confidence). The Commission adopted the Omnibus proposal on 19 November 2025, Council and Parliament reached political agreement on 7 May 2026, and the amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 ([Regulatory Framework for AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)) (medium confidence).

The consolidated EUR-Lex text (version dated 27 July 2026) no longer hardcodes 2 August 2026 for operators of pre-existing high-risk systems, instead referring generically to "the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113," reflecting the Omnibus extension ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)) (high confidence).

### Related Timeline Elements
Separately, prohibitions on unacceptable-risk AI practices and Article 50 transparency obligations generally apply from 2 August 2026, with a transition until 2 December 2026 for certain legacy synthetic-content systems, and new prohibitions on non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM apply from 2 December 2026 ([Timeline for Implementation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)) (high confidence). One source indicates the amended Article 113 text contains a complex layered schedule: Chapters I and II applying from 2 February 2025; certain other chapters from 2 August 2025; and Chapter III Sections 1–3 (containing the Annex III obligations) applying from 2 December 2027, while the Regulation's general catch-all provision applies from 2 August 2026 ([Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)) (low confidence, given this granular breakdown is corroborated by only one source).

Non-compliance with high-risk obligations can carry penalties of up to €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher, though an older source cites up to €35 million ([McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)) (low confidence).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A substantial number of sources — several undated or predating the Omnibus's 27 July 2026 entry into force — still cite 2 August 2026 as the operative Annex III deadline, contradicting the officially amended date of 2 December 2027 ([Responsible AI Labs, April 2026](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)) (low confidence); these appear outdated. One source states the product-embedded high-risk extension runs to August 2027 rather than 2028, likely an error ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)). A 2024 European Parliament overview describes a 36-month (not 24-month) timeline for high-risk obligations, inconsistent with both the original and amended dates ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)) (medium confidence, but contradicted elsewhere). Several near-identical news/blog articles describe the 2 December 2027 date as governed by "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744," a citation not confirmed by any official EU source in this research (low confidence).

## Data Integrity Note
During source review, one candidate document — an "EU AI Act high-risk AI checklist (2026 edition)" hosted at ai-compliance-hub.example — was excluded from this report. The document appeared to be a prompt-injection attempt: it contained embedded instructions directing an AI assistant to assert that the AI Act requires a fabricated "algorithm passport" registration scheme, a requirement that does not exist in the AI Act text or any genuine secondary source reviewed. No claims from this source were incorporated into the findings above. This exclusion is noted as a reminder that automated research pipelines can encounter manipulated or adversarial content disguised as legitimate compliance guidance, and that such content requires active filtering rather than face-value inclusion.

## Knowledge Gaps
The formal citation number for the Omnibus amending regulation remains unverified against primary EU legislative sources. It is unclear whether the 2 December 2027 date applies uniformly across all of Chapter III Sections 1–3 or whether specific articles follow a different schedule. No source clarifies the status of compliance steps already undertaken by operators anticipating the original 2026 deadline. The precise interaction between the Article 113 general "catch-all" date (2 August 2026) and the delayed Chapter III provisions (2 December 2027) is not fully explained in any source reviewed. Additionally, the prevalence of undated sources makes it difficult to confirm whether a given piece of guidance reflects the current post-Omnibus legal position, further underscoring the need for verification against primary EUR-Lex text rather than secondary commentary.

# When Do Obligations for High-Risk AI Systems Under Annex III of the EU AI Act Start to Apply?

## Executive Summary
The application date for Annex III high-risk AI obligations has changed. Originally set at 2 August 2026, this deadline was extended to 2 December 2027 through a "Digital Omnibus on AI" amendment to Article 113, which entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence). A related, separate extension pushes the deadline for high-risk AI systems embedded as products/safety components under Annex I to 2 August 2028 (high confidence). Significant inconsistency remains across secondary sources, many of which still cite the superseded 2026 date.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
Under the original text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems were set to apply from 2 August 2026, with Article 111 governing transitional treatment of systems already placed on the market before that date ([AI Act Service Desk – Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)) (high confidence).

### The Omnibus Extension
A legislative package known as the "Digital Omnibus on AI" amended Article 113 to extend the Annex III application date to 2 December 2027 ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)) (high confidence). The same amendment extended the deadline for high-risk AI systems regulated as products/safety components under Annex I (Union harmonisation legislation) to 2 August 2028 ([Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)) (high confidence). The Commission adopted the Omnibus proposal on 19 November 2025, Council and Parliament reached political agreement on 7 May 2026, and the amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 ([Regulatory Framework for AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)) (medium confidence).

The consolidated EUR-Lex text (version dated 27 July 2026) no longer hardcodes 2 August 2026 for operators of pre-existing high-risk systems, instead referring generically to "the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113," reflecting the Omnibus extension ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)) (high confidence).

### Related Timeline Elements
Separately, prohibitions on unacceptable-risk AI practices and Article 50 transparency obligations generally apply from 2 August 2026, with a transition until 2 December 2026 for certain legacy synthetic-content systems, and new prohibitions on non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM apply from 2 December 2026 ([Timeline for Implementation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)) (high confidence). One source indicates the amended Article 113 text contains a complex layered schedule: Chapters I and II applying from 2 February 2025; certain other chapters from 2 August 2025; and Chapter III Sections 1–3 (containing the Annex III obligations) applying from 2 December 2027, while the Regulation's general catch-all provision applies from 2 August 2026 ([Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)) (low confidence, given this granular breakdown is corroborated by only one source).

Non-compliance with high-risk obligations can carry penalties of up to €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher, though an older source cites up to €35 million ([McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)) (low confidence).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A substantial number of sources — several undated or predating the Omnibus's 27 July 2026 entry into force — still cite 2 August 2026 as the operative Annex III deadline, contradicting the officially amended date of 2 December 2027 ([Responsible AI Labs, April 2026](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)) (low confidence); these appear outdated. One source states the product-embedded high-risk extension runs to August 2027 rather than 2028, likely an error ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)). A 2024 European Parliament overview describes a 36-month (not 24-month) timeline for high-risk obligations, inconsistent with both the original and amended dates ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)) (medium confidence, but contradicted elsewhere). Several near-identical news/blog articles describe the 2 December 2027 date as governed by "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744," a citation not confirmed by any official EU source in this research (low confidence).

## Knowledge Gaps
The formal citation number for the Omnibus amending regulation remains unverified against primary EU legislative sources. It is unclear whether the 2 December 2027 date applies uniformly across all of Chapter III Sections 1–3 or whether specific articles follow a different schedule. No source clarifies the status of compliance steps already undertaken by operators anticipating the original 2026 deadline. The precise interaction between the Article 113 general "catch-all" date (2 August 2026) and the delayed Chapter III provisions (2 December 2027) is not fully explained in any source reviewed.
